_note: TOGETHER (session P2b, GDD 4.10 decision 6 'P2b's questions'; format in README.md). Sender: dating = the person you are together with (RomanceSystem; thread together), ex = someone you were together with. Everything is texting, time together, a day out: nothing more. Every storylet is guarded by the `romance` condition (and says nothing about a partner when there is none). The invitations land in a WEEKEND slot with the activity partner (Saturday or Sunday): going is time together (closeness, the moods, no neglect), staying home costs a little. The two beats are the rare real choices (a dinner, meeting the parents). Texts are written for a day ahead ('on {weekday}') and use {they} / {them} / {their} for the sender (she/her/her, he/him/his). Fictional minors.

text: Good morning. I dreamed we were at the lake and you were running with a hat on. Have a good day.
Morning. I have a double lesson first and no coffee. Think of me.
Good morning, runner. The bus is late again and it is raining. See you soon.
I saw your result. I am proud of you, whatever the number says.
I looked up your result as soon as I could. You did the thing you train for. I am glad I know you.
Good luck with the test tomorrow. You know more than you think you do.
You have a test tomorrow. Sleep, eat something, and it will be fine.
I saw your result. Congratulations. I hope you are doing well.
Good race. I still follow the results, you know. Take care.
There is a film I have wanted to see at the cinema, on {weekday} afternoon. Come with me?
Film on {weekday}? I will buy the popcorn, you pick the seats.

replies.label: Yes, let's go
replies.result: You sat in the back row and neither of you remembers the plot.

text: A long walk by the water on {weekday} morning? I will bring a flask of coffee.
The leaves are doing their thing. Walk in the forest on {weekday}? No watch, no pace.

replies.label: I would love that
replies.result: No watch, no pace. It was the best easy day of the month.

replies.label: I need the day to rest

text: We both have a pile of homework. Let's do it together at mine on {weekday}, and eat afterwards.
Sunday homework at my place on {weekday}? It always goes faster with someone next to you.

replies.label: Yes, bring the books
replies.hint: a day with {from}; grades ▲ a little
replies.result: You studied for two hours and ate for one.

replies.label: I will do it alone
replies.result: Fine. I will survive, I think.

text: My friends are meeting at the park on {weekday} and they keep asking about you. Come and meet them.
Come to the park on {weekday}. My friends want to see the runner I keep talking about.

replies.label: I will come
replies.hint: a late night; a day with {from}
replies.result: Everyone was nice. You got home late, with a smile you could not take off.

replies.label: I will come for a while
replies.result: An hour was enough to be liked.

replies.label: Not this time
replies.result: They will ask again. I will tell them you are shy.

text: We have been together for two months. I want to make it a proper Saturday: dinner, just us. Or if you would rather, a quiet day at home with a film. You decide.
Two months! Do you want to celebrate on Saturday? A restaurant, or pizza at my place, whichever you prefer.

replies.label: A proper dinner
replies.result: You both dressed up and felt silly about it, which was the best part.

replies.label: A quiet day at home
replies.result: Pizza and a film. Honestly, perfect.

text: My parents asked if you would come to Sunday dinner. They would like to meet you. They are nicer than they sound, I promise.
Mum has been asking about you for weeks. Sunday dinner at ours? There will be a lot of food and one embarrassing photo.

replies.label: I will come
replies.result: They were kind, and the photo was worse than promised.

replies.label: Not yet, but soon
replies.result: Okay. I will tell them you are busy training.
